title: Reason Code 22 — EAP type cannot be processed
plain_english: The client asked for an EAP method that this NPS server couldn't run for this connection. Very often this isn't about the client at all: if the NPS server's own certificate is broken or missing, PEAP can't even initialize, and every client gets this error regardless of what it requests.

causes.cause: The NPS server certificate is missing, expired, or lost its private key, so PEAP/EAP-TLS cannot start. If ALL clients started failing at once, start here.
causes.next_check: Open the network policy → Constraints → Authentication Methods → PEAP → Edit: does it still show a valid certificate? Also check the computer certificate store on the NPS server for expiry.

causes.cause: Client and policy disagree on the EAP method — the device is configured for EAP-TLS while the policy only offers PEAP-MSCHAPv2, or vice versa.
causes.next_check: Compare the 'EAP Type' field in this event with the EAP types listed in the matched network policy's constraints.

causes.cause: The EAP configuration blob in the policy is corrupted — a known aftermath of certificate renewals and NPS config imports.
causes.next_check: In the policy's PEAP settings, remove and re-add the EAP type, reselect the server certificate, and save.
